sourceChecks.claim: Inspected MySQL what-is-MySQL relational and client/server description; separate SQL server/backends/clients support the flow and shared structured data, with design choices remaining application-specific.

Inspected COMMIT documentation default autocommit, explicit START TRANSACTION and rollback of transactional tables; InnoDB flush-log-at-trx-commit followup confirms default per-commit flush, weakened settings and hardware assumptions. HTTP effects lie outside database rollback.

Inspected clustered/secondary-index page: clustered row data, PK fallback and repeated PK columns; scan-avoidance and deadlock/index followups support EXPLAIN, broad/small table scans, fewer searched locks and workload-dependent index cost.

Inspected point-in-time recovery full-backup-then-incremental-log model. Replaying only retained necessary history to a stop point requires a compatible base; live replication propagates deletes. Restore testing is a valid necessary verification step, not an asserted engine guarantee.
